questions.q: A web server crashes and automatically restarts every four minutes. At any random moment you check it, it's almost always up. What does this scenario best illustrate?
options: The system is both highly available and highly reliable
The system can appear highly available while being unreliable, since it doesn't keep working correctly over time
The system has no single point of failure
The system is practicing graceful degradation
questions.explain: Checking the system at a random instant shows it 'up' most of the time (high availability), but repeatedly crashing mid-use means it doesn't keep working correctly over a stretch of time — poor reliability.

options: A system that never experiences component failures
A system that keeps producing correct results even when some of its components fail
A measurement of how many nines of uptime a system has
The process of adding more RAM to a single machine
questions.explain: Fault tolerance isn't about preventing failure — it's about continuing to produce correct results despite some parts failing.

questions.q: What is the core mechanism distributed systems use to achieve fault tolerance and reliability?
options: Load balancing requests across stateless servers
Vertical scaling of the primary database server
Replication: keeping multiple synchronized copies of data or state across machines
Reducing the number of features a system offers
questions.explain: Replication keeps synchronized copies of data on separate machines so that if one fails, another already holds the same correct state and can keep serving results.

questions.q: A database has three replicas, but every write must first pass through a single coordinator process with no backup. What does this scenario demonstrate?
options: The replicas are now unnecessary and should be removed
Redundancy must be complete — an unreplicated coordinator upstream is a single point of failure that undermines the replicated database behind it
This configuration guarantees five-nines availability
This is an example of graceful degradation
questions.explain: Having replicas doesn't help if something feeding them is itself a single point of failure — reliability requires checking every layer, not just the obvious one.

options: Shutting the entire system down safely when any component fails
Losing some non-essential functionality during a failure while essential functionality keeps working, rather than a total outage
Gradually reducing a server's CPU allocation over time
A synonym for vertical scaling
questions.explain: Graceful degradation means a failure in a non-essential part (like a recommendation engine) shouldn't take down essential functions like search or checkout — partial functionality beats a total outage.
